extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia editors and contributors (new and experienced)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and editing Wikipedia content emphasizing that Wikipedia is an online encyclopedia, not a news outlet: what belongs, sourcing, neutrality, and avoiding original reporting or personal opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wikipedia is not a newspaper
rubrics_metrics.description: Wikipedia is an online encyclopedia, not a newspaper or online news site; it does not function as a journal of current news, nor does it disseminate the personal opinions of its contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most newspapers report current events and may include subjective opinion or investigative scoops; Wikipedia should not. The page stresses that Wikipedia is written from a neutral point of view and based on reliable sources and objectivity. It also points editors to Wikinews for news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat Wikipedia as a journal of current news
rubrics_metrics.description: There is usually no need to write articles about things with no historical significance; avoid creating articles that are merely transient news or trivia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reflecting current news on Wikipedia, ask whether the addition is truly encyclopedic and important or mere trivia. The essay references the phenomenon of recentism and links to Wikipedia:Recentism for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wikipedians are not journalists / do not provide primary reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Wikipedia does not offer firsthand reports of current events and is not a primary source for original reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions should not be treated as original journalism; editors should not present firsthand accounts as if Wikipedia were a news outlet. See Wikipedia:No original research for rules against primary reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: No original research
rubrics_metrics.description: Wikipedia is not a publisher of original thought; contributions must be based on information already published in reliable sources rather than on editors' own investigations or scoops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you uncover a 'scoop', you must first publish it in a reliable, reviewable source (e.g., an independent newspaper) before using it on Wikipedia. Attempts to publish unverifiable scoops on Wikipedia may be reverted as violations of the no original research policy; see WP:NOR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiability
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions must be verifiable: anyone should be able to check the facts for themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are expected to cite reliable sources for their contributions. Unverifiable claims or content lacking reliable references are subject to removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reliable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Content must be based on reliable sources rather than anonymous tips or unreviewed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay emphasizes that material should be based on reliable, reviewable sources; independent media coverage is required before using certain information (e.g., scoops) in Wikipedia articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral point of view (NPOV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles should be written from a neutral point of view and not present the personal viewpoints of the contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Injecting personal opinion into articles is unacceptable and may be treated as vandalism. The requirement for NPOV applies to article content and (to an extent) to user pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use Wikipedia as a soapbox / avoid personal opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Wikipedia is not a forum for contributors to disseminate their personal opinions or use article or user pages as platforms for advocacy or soapboxing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay warns that many Wikipedians frown on using user pages or subpages to spread opinions; user pages are intended to aid in building the encyclopedia. Editors are directed to other sites if they wish to express opinions publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite your sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to provide citations for their contributions so that claims are verifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay explicitly states 'We expect you to cite your sources for your contributions.' Lack of citations can lead to reversion of content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Wikinews for news content
rubrics_metrics.description: Wikinews is the Wikimedia project intended for news reporting and should be used for original news coverage rather than Wikipedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay notes Wikinews's mission statement and points editors toward that project for news-related work, distinguishing it from Wikipedia's encyclopedic purpose.
